items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Edgar, myself and an amateur alto player named Alex Baker, used to rehearse at Edgar's house or Alex's house twice every week.

ctx.x: I was given a weeks vacation without pay from the Western Union and it was just at the time the encampment was taking place. I had spoke about the encampment to William Smith, called Smittie by everyone, and a young man named Edgar Courance, who was a beginner on clarinet. He also lived on Carlisle Avenue, and I used to carry notes to him from a girl named Annie Jones when I was 14, and lived on Hathaway Street. Edgar was only one year older than I, but he was the kind of teenager that started liking girls when…

Edgar, myself and an amateur alto player named Alex Baker, used to rehearse at Edgar's house or Alex's house twice every week. I dont remember how I met Alex but I remember that he lived on Court Street. We could get orchestrations from a couple of music publishing stores up town and one we received was "Three O'clock In The Morning", which was a waltz. There was one place in this number where the trumpet part went as high as A above the staff and that was a note I could not reach, so I made a turn on the note…

My reading started to get better when a piano player named Clarence Trotter joined out little rehearsals. He would play the number while we looked over the parts. Then we'd play them slowly until we had a good idea how the notes sounded. Then we'd give the tempo a little lift, and then a little more until we had the number up to speed.
